settings.dnsPrimaryDesc: Where nodes send lookups the cache can't answer. An IPv6 address works too; it's still asked for A records.
settings.dnsSecondaryDesc: Used when the primary doesn't answer.
settings.dnsCacheDesc: How many names a node keeps in memory. All clients on the node share the cache.
settings.dnsTtlDesc: The shortest and longest time an answer stays in the cache.
settings.dnsStaleDesc: An expired answer is sent right away and refreshed in the background. 0 turns this off.
settings.blockDesc: For clients with ad blocking on, names on the lists you pick here get no answer. Pick one main list, then add TIF on top for malware and phishing. Each node downloads the lists itself, keeps a copy on disk, and swaps in a new copy only once it has downloaded in full, so a broken download never replaces a good list.
settings.blockPartial: Partly covered: orange is the least, yellow more, green the most
settings.blockAllow: Never blocked. A name here covers its subdomains too, and names with a custom record are never blocked either.
settings.blockAllowNone: No exceptions, so everything on the lists is blocked.
settings.dnsNoRecords: No custom records. Every lookup goes to the upstreams.
settings.restartingDesc: Applying your changes. The panel will be back in a moment.
settings.pageSizeDesc: Rows per page in the clients table. 0 shows them all.
settings.mtuDesc: The largest packet a node carries for a client.
settings.statsSecondsDesc: How often a node reads its traffic counters, in seconds. 0 turns it off.
settings.expireTimeDiffDesc: How many days before a subscription expires to warn about it.
settings.poolDesc: The range connected clients get their addresses from.
settings.echDesc: The name shown in the unencrypted part of the TLS handshake, like example.com. The real node name travels encrypted inside it. Nodes pick it up within seconds, clients on their next check. Leave it empty to turn ECH off.
settings.clientVersionDesc: The release every client on the network should run. A client one release behind can put the update off; anything older can't connect until it updates. Only releases signed with the update key are listed.
settings.clientVersionNoList: Couldn't load the releases from GitHub. The current choice stays as it is.
settings.congestionDesc: How nodes and clients pace their sending. BBR measures the connection and adapts to it. Brutal sends at one fixed rate no matter how much is lost. Changing this restarts the nodes, and every tunnel reconnects.
settings.brutalDesc: Sends at this many Mbit/s regardless of loss. Keep it below the slowest client's connection: a client on a slower line will keep losing its tunnel under load.
settings.bbrProfileDesc: Conservative ramps up slower and backs off when it overshoots. Standard is the stock behavior. Aggressive ramps up harder and holds a larger window.
settings.ipv6Desc: Gives clients an IPv6 address, AAAA answers, and access to IPv6-only sites through the nodes' own IPv6. Turn it on only if every node has reliable IPv6. With it off, clients stay on IPv4 and nodes talk to each other over IPv4. Changing this restarts the nodes.
settings.maxStreamsDesc: How many flows one connection can keep open at once. A browser alone can use hundreds, and on an exit node all clients share a single connection. Raise it ahead of your client count.
settings.streamWindowDesc: The starting and largest receive window of one flow, in kilobytes. A flow rides out packet loss without stalling when the largest window is about three times its bandwidth-delay product.
settings.connWindowDesc: The starting and largest receive window shared by all of one client's flows, in kilobytes.
settings.socketBufferDesc: How many kilobytes the node asks the kernel for on its listening socket. The kernel caps this at net.core.rmem_max.
settings.idleDesc: How many seconds a quiet connection is kept open, and how often it's pinged to stay open through NAT.
settings.refreshMinutesDesc: How often every client re-reads its subscription. A client that set its own interval keeps it.

sensorHint.mem: Alert when memory use goes over the threshold
sensorHint.disk: Alert when disk use goes over the threshold
sensorHint.sockets: Alert on an unusual number of open TCP sockets
sensorHint.udpSockets: Alert on an unusual number of open UDP sockets
sensorHint.clientOffline: Alert when a client that was online goes quiet for this many hours

notifications.backupReminderHint: Remind me to back up the database if it hasn't been backed up in this many days

update.requiredText: This version can no longer connect to the network. Update to keep using qd.

routing.everythingElseDesc: Select the connection type to be used by default

roleDesc.default: This role means that the global connection type selector will be used for the policy.
roleDesc.direct: This role means that the connection will not be routed through the tunnel into the qd network.
roleDesc.tunnel: This role means that the global connection type selector will be ignored for the policy.
roleDesc.egress: This role means that the connection will be routed through both ingress and egress nodes of qd network.
roleDesc.noEgress: This role means that the connection will be routed exclusively through the ingress node of the qd network.

routing.newFlowsNote: Routing policies allow you to precisely control routing based on defined roles. You can assign different routing policies to applications, source/destination IP addresses, or domains; you can also take advantage of pre-configured policy bundles without requiring in-depth knowledge of internet network architecture.
routing.matchNote: You simply select an application - for example, a web browser - and assign it a direct access role in the list; as a result, all connections made through that application will bypass the qd network.
routing.searchProcess_phone: Search for apps by name or package
routing.noProcesses: No running app has an open connection.
routing.noProcesses_phone: No apps or app packages to show.
routing.byNameHint: Apply to all apps matches with this name
routing.restartNeededDesc: Android OS applies some policies only when the connection starts, so these take effect after a reconnect to the qd network.
routing.restartNeededIdle: Android OS applies some policies only when the connection starts, so these take effect when you connect to the qd network.
routing.resetRulesDesc: Removes all app policies and sets connection type to default. Domain policies and bundles will not be removed.
routing.domainHint: A domain routing policy covers the domain and all its subdomains.
routing.domainTaken: Routing policy is already applied to this domain.
routing.domainNote: A domain routing policy covers the domain and all its subdomains. It applies to apps without a policy of their own and before the bundles.
routing.resetProcessDesc: Removes all app policies and sets connection type to default. Domain policies and bundles will not be removed.
routing.resetDomainsDesc: Removes all domain policies. App and bundle policies will not be removed.
routing.resetBundlesDesc: Removes all bundle policies. App and domain policies will not be removed.
routing.bundleNote: A bundle is a ready-made list of the sites and addresses of a group of services. It applies only when neither the app nor the domain has a routing policy of its own.

settings.autostart: Launch qd when the device turns on

settings.manualBehaviourDesc: What qd does when you start it yourself. If it's already running, opening it again just shows the window.

settings.relayNone: No relays yet. Paste a vless:// link below.
settings.relayNoneForced: Forcing relay sends all traffic through a relay, but you haven't added one yet.
settings.navLowDesc: Move the navigation buttons to a floating bar at the bottom.
settings.themeDesc: Switch it with the button at the top, or match the OS setting.
